messages:
Sam Support: Flagging an escalation 3:45 UTC — multiple enterprise customers in us-west observed large API latencies and intermittent 504s. p95 jumped from ~110ms to ~460ms; p99 spikes near 2.1s. Ticket #4521 reopened.
Maya SRE: Acknowledged. Any recent deployments or infra windows around that time?
Sam Support: The night window completed shortly before the spike. No app deploys, but infra ran a small kernel canary and an NVMe firmware push last night.
metrics-bot: Alert: routing-service.latency.p95 > 400ms (cluster: us-west-2) between 03:40-04:05 UTC. Error rate rose 0.7% -> 3.0%.
Arjun Infra: I see a queued GPU driver update to CUDA 536.12 and a kernel 6.6 canary applied to a subset of gw-rt pool. Were specific hosts called out?
Sam Support: Customer provided traces from their requests hitting gw-rt-uw2-09 and gw-rt-uw2-11. They included request traces showing backend queue times high.
Maya SRE: SSHing gw-rt-uw2-09 now. Running `dmesg | tail -n 50` shows repeated nvme timeouts and controller resets: 
```
[  987.654321] nvme 0000:81:00.0: completion timeout
[  988.123456] nvme nvme0: controller reset
```
Maya SRE: `iostat -x 1 5` shows %util hitting 99% and avg await jumping to 110ms during bursts.
Arjun Infra: That smells like storage-side contention. Did we change NVMe firmware recently?
Maya SRE: Yes, we rolled NVMe firmware 5.8.23 to a batch including these hosts two nights ago as part of perf tuning. Those hosts also have kernel 6.6 applied in the canary.
Alex Runtime: Important: when NVMe controller resets occur, runtime's KV cache writes stall and that backpressure increases model token latencies. p99s can go through roof.
Jen Oncall: Can we repro on an isolated node (non-prod) with the same kernel+FW combo? I can run a synthetic inference burst and fio to stress IO.
Arjun Infra: I'll provision a clone with kernel6.6 + NVMe FW 5.8.23 and run a repro. Also prepping rollback playbook for NVMe FW to 5.7.09 if we confirm regression.
metrics-bot: host_io.latency_p99 for gw-rt-uw2-09 = 520ms at 03:41 UTC.
Maya SRE: Running `fio --name=randrw --iodepth=64 --rw=randrw --bs=4k --numjobs=8 --runtime=90` on spare device: we're seeing 99th percentile > 350ms and intermittent controller resets.
Sam Support: Customers are asking for a timeline and stop-gap. We need to divert traffic away from impacted hosts asap.
Alex Runtime: Short-term mitigations: 1) Drain affected gw-rt nodes and route traffic to healthy hosts, 2) Temporarily lower batch sizes and disable aggressive prefix/KV sync to reduce IO pressure, 3) Put per-customer circuit breakers to prevent cascading queuing.
Maya SRE: Draining gw-rt-uw2-09/11 and shifting traffic now.
deploy-bot: Rebalancer: shifted 22% of traffic off gw-rt-uw2-09/11 to other nodes in the pool.
Sam Support: Notifying impacted customers that we've diverted traffic and are investigating.
Arjun Infra: Repro results: with kernel6.6 + NVMe FW 5.8.23 we reproduce fio high tails and `dmesg` shows nvme resets. With kernel6.6 + NVMe FW 5.7.09 the issue does not reproduce.
Alex Runtime: Evidence points to NVMe firmware 5.8.23 regressing with kernel 6.6's IO stack changes. GPU driver (CUDA) doesn't appear required to trigger this, but keep it in scope if we see related artifacts.
Jen Oncall: Action plan?
Arjun Infra: Immediate: staged rollback of NVMe firmware on affected hosts to 5.7.09. I'll run on one host first as a test, then roll 4-at-a-time during off-peak. Owner: Arjun. ETA: initial rollback test within 60 minutes.
Maya SRE: I'll keep those nodes drained and monitor the traffic shift. After a successful rollback test we'll reintroduce nodes slowly. Expect p95 to fall back within ~10-15min after a healthy node rejoins.
Sam Support: I'll update ticket #4521 and customers with the rollback plan and ETA.
metrics-bot: Observed improvement on test node gw-rt-uw2-09 after FW rollback to 5.7.09: p95 ~130ms, p99 < 400ms within 12 minutes. No new nvme reset messages in dmesg.
Arjun Infra: Proceeding with staged rollback across remaining impacted hosts (batch size 4). Coordinating windows with SRE.
Alex Runtime: Recommend adding a compatibility gate to our firmware rollout pipeline to prevent NVMe FW pushes to hosts running kernel >=6.6 until validated. Also add a canary workload test covering random RW patterns to the FW pipeline.
Maya SRE: I'll author the postmortem: timeline, reproducer steps (fio command, dmesg patterns), root cause (NVMe FW 5.8.23 incompatible with kernel 6.6 causing controller resets under bursty RW), short-term mitigations, and longer-term rollout safeguards.
Jen Oncall: I'll update oncall runbook with the reproduce steps and the rapid-mitigation checklist (drain, rollback FW, reduce batch size).
Sam Support: Customer updated and monitoring notes added. We'll keep ticket open until postmortem posted.
Arjun Infra: Completed rollbacks queued; monitoring shows steady regressions resolved.
Maya SRE: Final check: I'll attach dashboards showing p95/p99 before/after and paste the repro logs into the incident tracker. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
